title: The fall of the Berlin Wall, 1989 — opened by a mistake at a press conference
sources: Wikipedia: Fall of the Berlin Wall — on 9 November 1989 the Krenz-led Politburo decided East Germans could cross directly, including between East and West Berlin; the new regulations were to take effect the next day; Günter Schabowski, the regime's spokesman, was handed a note from Krenz shortly before his press conference with no instructions on how to handle it; at the end he read it out; a reporter asked when it would take effect; after a few seconds' hesitation Schabowski replied 'As far as I know, it takes effect immediately, without delay'; he ended the press conference at 19:00; excerpts led West German news (ZDF 19:17, ARD 20:00 Tagesschau: 'The GDR has announced that, starting immediately, its borders are open to everyone'); crowds gathered at the Wall; at 23:30 Stasi officer Harald Jäger decided to open the gates at the Bornholmer Straße crossing; the crowds vastly outnumbered the border guards; East Berliners were greeted with flowers and champagne; people called Mauerspechte (wallpeckers) chipped off souvenirs; the Wall opened after 28 years
Wikipedia: Günter Schabowski — he improvised a slightly mistaken answer that seemed to announce the Wall's immediate end
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1985 Garry Kasparov, aged 22, becomes the youngest world chess champion; 1914 HMAS Sydney defeats SMS Emden at the Cocos Islands

Photos (public domain / CC0): Berliners on the Wall, people with a pickaxe, crossing at the Wall, 10 November 1989; East German policemen at the Brandenburg Gate (US DoD); a crane removing part of the Wall at the Brandenburg Gate; the Wall in 1961 and in 1990; an escape in 1961 (CIA); Kennedy in Berlin, 1963; Berlin at night from the ISS
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): television screens, a champagne bottle opening, fireworks

post.facebook:
On this night in 1989, the Berlin Wall opened — because of a misread note.

East Germany's leaders had decided to let citizens cross the border more freely, starting the next day. Party spokesman Günter Schabowski was handed the note just before a live press conference, with no instructions. He read it out. A reporter asked when it took effect. After a few seconds' hesitation, he said: "As far as I know… immediately, without delay."

West German television broadcast it that evening: the border was open. Thousands rushed to the crossings. The guards had no orders. At 11:30 pm, at Bornholmer Straße, Stasi officer Harald Jäger opened the gates. East Berliners poured through and were met with flowers and champagne — and by morning, people were chipping the Wall apart with hammers.

Also on 9 November: Garry Kasparov became world chess champion at 22 (1985), and HMAS Sydney caught the raider Emden (1914).

youtube.description:
9 November 1989: East Germany planned to ease border crossings from the next day. Spokesman Günter Schabowski, handed the note without instructions, read it at a live press conference — and when asked when it took effect, answered "As far as I know, immediately, without delay." TV reported the border was open, crowds rushed the crossings, and at 11:30 pm Stasi officer Harald Jäger opened the gates at Bornholmer Straße. After 28 years, the Berlin Wall was open.

Also on 9 November: Kasparov becomes world champion (1985) and the Emden is caught (1914).
